title: Best Nursing and Maternity Bras UK
short: Eight maternity and nursing bras tested by pregnant and breastfeeding women, from a budget 3-pack to seamless premium styles.
intro: A nursing bra needs to grow with a changing bust through pregnancy and breastfeeding while staying comfortable day and night. This guide is based on Mumsnet's tested roundup (updated June 2026), where a panel of verified pregnant women and mothers of babies under two tried bras during pregnancy, breastfeeding and the first year, cross-referenced against historic testing and advice from breastfeeding charity La Leche League and bra-fitting expert Tracey-Jane Hughes. Prices shown are those quoted by Mumsnet at time of writing.

products.name: Emma-Jane Padded Seamless Maternity & Nursing Bra
products.best_for: Maximum adjustability as your shape changes through pregnancy and beyond
products.key_spec: Six back adjusters with three clips each, removable pads, dual-layer cups, non-wired, S-XL (B-DD)
products.summary: Mumsnet's tester Laura wore it from her second trimester through two years of breastfeeding and said the clips were a lifesaver, staying in place far better than other nursing bras that kept unclipping. She loved it so much she bought a few, calling it one of the best on the market for value. Super-stretchy material allows for maximum expansion, with a seam-free finish and lace trim.
pros: Six back adjusters for maximum adjustability
Removable padding and dual-layer cups for support
Clips stay in place well during feeding
cons: Quite pricey for a single bra
products.search: JoJo Maman Bebe Emma-Jane Padded Seamless Maternity Nursing Bra

products.name: 2-Pack Padded Cotton Nursing Bras
products.best_for: Comfortable, affordable everyday nursing bras in a modern style
products.key_spec: 95% cotton, adjustable straps, clip and drop-down cups, non-wired, sizes 32-38 (A-DD)
products.summary: The most recommended maternity bra among Mumsnet's recent tester panel. Tester Sarah praised the comfort and style, saying many maternity bras looked frumpy but these kept a modern look. Mum-of-two Beccy found them easy to adjust and simple to clip and unclip for breastfeeding, and tester Lizzie liked that they're non-wire and reasonably priced. Sizing doesn't go beyond 38DD, and the design is quite basic.

specs.Price guide: £18 for two (at time of writing, was £23)

pros: Inexpensive multi-pack
Soft, comfortable cotton jersey
Good choice of colourways
products.search: H&M MAMA 2-Pack Padded Cotton Nursing Bras

products.name: Full Cup Maternity Bra
products.best_for: A stylish bra that doesn't show under clothing and lasts for years
products.key_spec: Cotton and modal blend, triangle cups, drop-down nursing clips, non-wired, XS-XL
products.summary: Mumsnet's tester Becky found it looks nicer than most maternity bras and it's easy to get a boob out to feed discreetly. She called it great value for money as it lasted years without stretching too much or losing shape, despite her body changing during and after pregnancy, and kept wearing it years after she stopped breastfeeding because it was so comfy. It's pricey at full price and can run small.
pros: Soft, breathable cotton, very comfortable
Triangle cups don't show under clothing
Kept its stretch even after years of use
products.search: Calvin Klein Full Cup Maternity Bra

products.name: Maternity Nursing Bras, 3-pack
products.best_for: Comfortable, no-frills bras for sleeping and nursing on a tight budget
products.key_spec: 95% cotton, pull-down cups, no hooks or underwire, sizes M-XXL (34B-40D)
products.summary: A soft, budget pack that won't win style points but reviewers rave about the comfort, which matters most for breast or nipple tenderness during pregnancy. Pull-down cups (rather than clips) work well for night feeds, there's space for breast pads, and there are no clasps, hooks or underwires to dig in. Not very supportive, and sizing doesn't include a smaller A cup.
pros: Cheap and comfortable
Wire-free
Good for sleeping and nursing in bed
cons: Sizing doesn't include a smaller A cup

products.name: Jasmine Lace Trim Maternity Nursing Bra, 2-pack
products.best_for: A reliable, machine-washable everyday bra across a wide size range
products.key_spec: Moulded cups with lace trim, cotton-lined, non-wired, sizes 32-42 (B-G)
products.summary: One Mumsnetter said these were the best she'd found recently, still wearing them two years later, and appreciated being able to order a range of M&S sizes online and return what doesn't fit. It's essentially a good T-shirt bra with moulded cups and a lace trim; the nursing clips worked well and the cotton lining feels comfy with no irritation. Machine-washable at 40 degrees, with milk stains easy to remove. It doesn't have much 'wow factor'.

specs.Price guide: £13 for two (at time of writing, was £25)

pros: Great range of sizing
Machine-washable and affordable
Reliable brand with easy returns
cons: Not much 'wow factor', but does the job
products.search: M&S Jasmine Lace Trim Maternity Nursing Bra

products.name: Body Silk Seamless Nursing Bra
products.best_for: A smooth silhouette under fitted clothing with all-day comfort
products.key_spec: Four-way-stretch fabric, removable foam inserts, B-clip converter for later, non-wired, XS-2XL
products.summary: Mumsnet's testers said it was so comfy they could happily wear it all day and even sleep in it. The seamless design gives a smooth silhouette with good separation under clothes, a favourite of one pregnant tester under maternity workwear, and cups fold down fully for feeding without rummaging. The small size range felt forgiving as bodies changed. It's difficult to adjust once on, and testers found the foam inserts unflattering and better left out.
pros: Very comfy, stretchy fabric moulds to the body
Easy to wash and dries fast
Comes with a B-clip converter to use as an ordinary bra later
products.search: Bravado Body Silk Seamless Nursing Bra

products.name: Keep Cool Sleep Seamless Maternity and Nursing Bra
products.best_for: Women who want a bra at night without digging straps or overheating
products.key_spec: Four-way Adaptive Stretch, breathable racerback panel, quick-dry, no hooks or clips, S-XXL
products.summary: A tester loved these for sheer comfort with no clipping needed. Designed for night wear, with a breathable back zone and quick-dry technology to ward off night sweats, plus plenty of give in the cups for breast pads. Support is minimal, which Mumsnet notes is fairly standard for a sleep bra, and some reviewers reported sizing being off.
pros: Adaptive Stretch technology grows with you
Breathable racerback design helps cool you down
Inexpensive
cons: Some reviewers reported sizing was off
products.search: Medela Keep Cool Sleep Seamless Maternity Nursing Bra

products.name: Show Off Lace Non Wired Nursing Bra
products.best_for: Fuller-busted women who want support without an underwire
products.key_spec: Sizes to 42H, hook and eye fastenings with 6 settings, cotton-lined cups, wire-free stretchy underband
products.summary: Mumsnet users praised the support: one said it isn't wired but hoists things back into place better than some others she's tried, and she was considering ordering another one. A large size range up to 42H, attractive design and cotton-lined cups add to the appeal, and it stays smooth under clothing thanks to A-frame support. It's pricey.
pros: Great range of sizes, up to 42H
Attractive design, smooth under clothing
A-frame support and cotton-lined cups

guide.q: Should I buy an underwired nursing bra?
guide.a: Most nursing bras, including all in this guide, are non-wired, since underwires can restrict milk ducts and increase the risk of blocked ducts or mastitis while breastfeeding. Support instead comes from wide bands and straps, as on the HOTmilk and JoJo Maman Bebé bras.

Clip-down cups, like the JoJo Maman Bebé Emma-Jane, tend to give a more secure fit and were praised for staying put. Pull-down cups, like the ZUMIY budget pack, are simpler for one-handed night feeds but can feel less supportive.

guide.q: How many nursing bras do I need?
guide.a: Budget multi-packs like the H&M MAMA or ZUMIY are a cheap way to build a rotation while your size is still changing, and Mumsnet suggests going budget early since bust size shifts a lot during and after pregnancy. Invest in one or two premium bras, like the Calvin Klein or Bravado, once your size settles.

guide.q: Do I need a separate bra for sleeping?
guide.a: Some women find a bra essential for comfort and support at night, especially while breastfeeding, others don't get on with them at all. If you want one, the Medela Keep Cool Sleep is designed specifically for night wear with cooling technology and minimal support.
